summary: the discretization error of a run's finer result, from the same quantity at two resolutions, and the value extrapolated to zero spacing

inputs.name: fine
inputs.meaning: the quantity from the run at the finer resolution, in its unit

inputs.name: coarse
inputs.meaning: the same quantity from the run at the coarser resolution, in the same unit

inputs.name: refinement_ratio
inputs.meaning: the coarse spacing over the fine one (a mesh size, a time step, a grid cell), above 1

inputs.name: order
inputs.meaning: the order of convergence of the scheme, the formal one or one observed over three resolutions; a row with its own source

outputs.name: estimated
outputs.meaning: true when an error was estimated; false, with why, when the inputs do not allow it

outputs.name: error
outputs.meaning: the estimated discretization error of the finer result, its magnitude, in the quantity's unit: the run's own numerical error the tolerance rule weighs

outputs.name: signed_correction
outputs.meaning: the finer result's difference from the extrapolated value, with its sign

outputs.name: extrapolated
outputs.meaning: the value extrapolated to zero spacing

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why no error was estimated, or null

validity: two runs of one scheme on the same problem in its asymptotic range, the quantity converging monotonically with the spacing at the order handed; higher-order terms are neglected, so the estimate is as good as that range holds. It says nothing of a modelling error, and judges nothing

source.citation: NASA Glenn Research Center, NPARC Alliance CFD Verification and Validation, Examining Spatial (Grid) Convergence (read 2026-11-18, https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/wind/valid/tutorial/spatconv.html; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261118-nasa-grc-spatial-convergence), after P. J. Roache's book it cites
source.locus: section Richardson Extrapolation: the generalized equation for a p-th order method and a grid ratio r = h2/h1, f(h=0) = f1 + (f1 - f2)/(r^p - 1), read off its image eq_rich2.gif; and the passage that takes its second term as an error estimator of f1

note: Made for the person's amended tolerance rule of 2026-11-18 ('Yes, run's own error', docs/ideas/20261118.md: the run's own numerical error, estimated from two resolutions or from a series' standard error), as a common skill of meta_agent/tasks/025; the series' standard error is standard_error_of_independent_estimates. No value of the source stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field.
